title: [YouPass Collect] - Australian doctors: gender and origin trends
prompt: The chart below gives information about doctors practicing in Australia over a 30-year period, including their gender and country of origin.
Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table and bar charts give information about the total number of doctors in Australia, their gender composition, and their countries of origin across three time points: 1986, 1996, and 2006.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the medical workforce in Australia grew considerably over the 30-year period. While Australian-trained doctors consistently outnumbered their foreign counterparts, the gender balance among practitioners fluctuated noticeably throughout the cited period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the size and gender composition of the workforce, there were 300,000 doctors in Australia in 1986, with males accounting for a slight majority at 55% compared to females at 45%. The total figure rose sharply to 640,000 by 1996 before continuing to climb to 800,000 in 2006, more than doubling over the entire period. Regarding gender, a reversal was observed in 1996, when female practitioners edged ahead at 56%, while males fell to 44%. However, by 2006, males had regained the majority at 52%, with females making up the remaining 48%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to the nationality breakdown, Australian doctors dominated the profession throughout, comprising 61% of the total in 1986, compared to 39% for those of other nationalities. This gap narrowed in 1996, when the share of Australian doctors dipped to 57% while foreign-trained practitioners rose to 43%. By 2006, however, the nationality ratio had returned to exactly its 1986 level, with Australian doctors once again accounting for 61% of the workforce and overseas-trained doctors making up the remaining 39%.
